chapter: Wagon bands, halls and the old brass bands
title: Playing outside the hall to draw the crowd
summary: Bands played a half-dozen numbers on the sidewalk in front of the hall, and girls would beg for another tune.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: And they'd get off the truck, on they'd get on the sidewalk in front of the hall, and they'd play that. And
then nobody asked where is the piano or who...
They would play out in front so they'd invite the people to come in.

Yeah. They'd play a little program out there, maybe a half-a-dozen numbers. They'd find a chick out there, the trumpet player or the clarinet player, who would ask them, "Play me another song before you all go in there. I ain't ready for you'all to come in there yet. I might go home and wash up and dress and come on and be out there with you...you know, the way I feel towards you. Please play me another tune."

The cat is going to be obliged to play another tune. Until the guy who is booking it says, "All right, that's enough out there. If they're coming, they're coming." Then someone says, "They ain't comin', they ain't comin'." "Come on in here, let's get this band going." Because the people inside would be waiting...
